bom.justification: Arduino Uno R3 MCU shared by 3 blocks — climate: Arduino Uno MCU reading the DHT22 on D2. The pin is bidirectional: it pulls DATA low for the start pulse, then listens.; alarm: Arduino Uno MCU switching the load from D8. The pin sources at most 3.66 mA into Q1's base over every part tolerance, under the 20 mA recommended per pin.; status: Arduino Uno MCU driving the LED from D13. Each GPIO is rated 20 mA recommended, 40 mA absolute; this design stays at or under 11.7 mA over every part tolerance.
bom.price_note: static catalogue price, recorded in the repository on 2026-07-25; when it was first observed is not recorded — not a distributor quote

bom.justification: DHT22: ±0.5 °C, ±2 %RH over a single-wire open-drain bus. It cannot be read faster than every 2 s, and without R1 its DATA line never goes high.
bom.price_note: static catalogue price, recorded in the repository on 2026-07-25; when it was first observed is not recorded — not a distributor quote

bom.justification: 10000Ω, the Aosong datasheet value, fast enough for 0.3 m of cable. Rise time ≈ 1.1 µs worst case; halving R1 halves it but doubles the 0.5 mA sunk while DATA is held low.
bom.price_note: static catalogue price, recorded in the repository on 2026-07-25; when it was first observed is not recorded — not a distributor quote

bom.justification: 100nF bypass across the shared rail at the MCU's supply pin, one for the board: every block's generator places one, and on one board they are the same part. Without it switching noise couples into every line on the board.
bom.price_note: static catalogue price, recorded in the repository on 2026-07-25; when it was first observed is not recorded — not a distributor quote

bom.justification: NPN low-side switch for the 30 mA load. It needs 3 mA of base current (I_C/10) to saturate at V_CE ≤ 0.3 V; it gets at least 3.04 mA. Under-driven, it would sit in its linear region and heat.
1210Ω, the largest E96 value that still saturates Q1 at the worst corner. Base current 3.04–3.66 mA; a larger R1 starves the base, a smaller one loads the pin for nothing.

Header for the load: pin 1 to the 5 V rail, pin 2 to Q1's collector. The value is the load's equivalent resistance as declared — 5 V at 30 mA — which is what the netlist models; it is not a part on the board.
Flyback diode across the load. When Q1 turns off, the load's inductance drives its 30 mA on through D1 instead of spiking Q1's collector past its 40 V rating.
Red LED, V_f 1.96 V at 9.95 mA on its fitted diode model (datasheet 1.7–2.4 V at 20 mA). A lower-V_f part in the same spread raises the current to 11.7 mA — still under its 30 mA rating.
280Ω, the E96 value nearest 10 mA. It sets I = (V_pin − V_f)/R1 ≈ 9.95 mA; halving it would roughly double the current and, past 20 mA, overload the pin.
